support-john: Hey SRE team — several customers reported p99 spikes for the text-gen API from eu-west-1 around 09:10 UTC. Customers see 600–1200ms extra per request, affects realtime flows. I attached a small probe summary and a customer cURL trace.

alex_sre: Thanks — can you paste the probe output or a snippet? any recent deploys? @chen_oncall are you on call? :eyes: 

support-john: pasted probe here (sanitized):
```
mtr -r -c 10 api.redwood.example -> eu-west1-edge
1. 10.1.0.1 0.7 ms
2. 52.30.10.7 2.1 ms
3. 34.200.17.9 8.4 ms
4. 91.198.35.22 45.7 ms  <-- large hop
5. 91.198.35.22 46.1 ms
6. 13.32.100.5 120.5 ms <-- cross-az bounce
```
curl --connect-timeout 2 -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
* TLS handshake takes ~300ms on repeated runs
```

vivian_net: I see concurrent DNS flaps for eu-west1 POP in our DNS metrics around 09:09–09:12 UTC, TTL re-resolves returned different anycast origins. Likely geo-reshuffle + a flaky peering. I'm pulling GSLB logs now.

chen_oncall: no prod deploys in that window per deploy-bot. deploy-bot: last canary finished 2026-03-17T08:55:12Z by infra/route-adjust.

deploy-bot: {deploy_id: infra/route-adjust, finished_at: 2026-03-17T08:55:12Z, regions: global} 

alex_sre: Ok looks network-y. Quick checklist: 1) confirm GSLB weights/health checks, 2) check peering e2e, 3) confirm TLS handshakes counts on edge (SNI mismatches?), 4) any config push to BGP/ASN from peer?

vivian_net: GSLB shows several origin switches for host api.redwood.example -> answers shifted from pop-a-eu to pop-c-eu then back. Some answers had path via peer-asn 65099 which has higher latency traces. TTLs were short (30s) so clients re-resolved mid-flow.

alex_sre: That aligns with customer repro. Mitigations: force clients to pinned POP via response header route-hint (short term) and increase TTL to 60s while we investigate (if Safe). Can we also enable local TLS session resumption caches to reduce handshake cost?

vivian_net: I pushed a temporary GSLB weight bias away from peer-asn 65099 at 09:25 UTC for 10m window. Also raised GSLB min TTL to 60s for api.* entries at 09:27 UTC. Monitoring now.

chen_oncall: enabled edge TLS session resumption cache bump on eu pops (LRU size +30%) at 09:30 UTC. Watching handshake latencies.

alex_sre: Good. Support, please tell affected customers we mitigated routing churn and are monitoring for 30m. Ask them to retry if they still see p99 > 500ms.

support-john: will notify now and include probe examples + ask for any client-side DNS caching behavior. :thumbsup:

vivian_net: Observability note — capture a sample of DNS answers and associated AS path for 09:05–09:35 window. I'll open a ticket for the peering team (PEER-1213) to engage the provider for AS 65099.

alex_sre: Post-mortem actions: 1) add runbook step for rapid GSLB biasing, 2) add automatic TTL bump on GSLB when origin churn detected, 3) add active probe to detect cross-az hairpin RTTS. Assign to eng-infra + eng-sre.

incidents-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0317-01: "eu-west1 DNS/peering-induced p99 spike" — severity: low, started_at: 2026-03-17T09:10:00Z, owner: vivian_net.

chen_oncall: current numbers after mitigations (09:45 UTC): p95 back to normal, p99 reduced ~70% vs peak. still seeing occasional 200–300ms TLS tails. continuing to monitor.

support-john: customers updated, one replied the flows are back to normal. closing initial escalation unless new reports come in. Thanks team. :heart:
